lesson: Diplomatic language & softening bad news (B2 · Aula 5)

cards.definition: A worry or a doubt that you raise politely about something.
cards.example:
- I have a small concern about the timeline, not about the budget.
Tenho uma pequena ressalva sobre o cronograma, não sobre o orçamento.
- Several stakeholders raised concerns about the new pricing model.
Vários stakeholders levantaram ressalvas sobre o novo modelo de preços.
- My main concern is that we are promising a date we do not control.
Minha principal preocupação é que estamos prometendo uma data que não controlamos.
cards.note: Raise a concern é levantar uma ressalva — o jeito diplomático de discordar sem dizer “I disagree”. Também funciona como verbo: that concerns me. Colocações úteis: a valid concern, address a concern.

cards.definition: A problem that delays progress without stopping it completely.
cards.example:
- The failed test was a setback, not a disaster.
O teste que falhou foi um revés, não um desastre.
- We had a minor setback in week two, and the schedule absorbed it.
Tivemos um revés pequeno na segunda semana, e o cronograma absorveu.
- After that setback, the board started asking for weekly updates.
Depois daquele contratempo, o conselho passou a pedir atualizações semanais.
cards.note: Palavra-chave para reenquadrar problemas: a temporary setback soa muito menos grave do que a failure. Aqui é substantivo; separado, set back é verbo: the strike set us back two weeks.

cards.definition: A little, in a small degree.
cards.example:
- We are slightly behind schedule — about three days.
Estamos levemente atrasados no cronograma — uns três dias.
- The forecast is slightly more conservative than last quarter's.
A projeção está um pouco mais conservadora que a do trimestre passado.
- I slightly disagree with the conclusion, although the data is solid.
Discordo um pouco da conclusão, embora os dados sejam sólidos.
cards.note: Suavizador clássico: slightly late, slightly over budget. Vem antes do adjetivo ou do comparativo. Em excesso soa evasivo, e o interlocutor passa a duvidar do número real.

cards.definition: Careful not to hurt or embarrass people when you say something difficult.
cards.example:
- Be tactful: say “challenging”, not “impossible”.
Seja diplomático: diga “desafiador”, não “impossível”.
- Her feedback was tactful but perfectly clear about the missed deadline.
O feedback dela foi diplomático, mas perfeitamente claro sobre o prazo perdido.
- A tactful message costs two extra minutes and saves two weeks of damage control.
Uma mensagem com tato custa dois minutos a mais e evita duas semanas de controle de danos.
cards.note: O substantivo é tact e o oposto é tactless (sem tato). Não confunda com tactical (tático). O advérbio é tactfully.

cards.definition: To say the same idea again with different words.
cards.example:
- Let me rephrase that: it is not wrong, it is incomplete.
Deixe-me reformular: não está errado, está incompleto.
- She rephrased the objection as a question, and the room relaxed.
Ela reformulou a objeção como pergunta, e a sala relaxou.
- If a sentence sounds harsh in writing, rephrase it before you send it.
Se uma frase soa dura por escrito, reformule antes de enviar.
cards.note: Let me rephrase that é o botão de refazer da conversa: conserta o tom sem admitir erro de conteúdo. Passado: rephrased. Parente próximo: reword.

cards.definition: To make something seem less serious or less important than it really is.
cards.example:
- Don't downplay the problem; soften the delivery, not the facts.
Não minimize o problema; suavize a entrega, não os fatos.
- He downplayed the churn numbers, and the board found out anyway.
Ele minimizou os números de churn, e o conselho descobriu do mesmo jeito.
- There is a thin line between being diplomatic and downplaying a risk.
Existe uma linha tênue entre ser diplomático e minimizar um risco.
cards.note: O contrário é play up (inflar). Passado: downplayed. Diplomacia mexe no tom; downplay mexe na importância do fato — por isso o segundo custa credibilidade.

cards.definition: To tell someone bad or important news for the first time.
cards.example:
- The manager had to break the news about the canceled project.
O gerente teve que dar a notícia sobre o projeto cancelado.
- I would rather break the news on a call than in a long email.
Prefiro dar a notícia numa ligação do que num e-mail longo.
- She broke the news to the client before the press release went out.
Ela deu a notícia ao cliente antes de o comunicado sair.
cards.note: A estrutura é break the news to somebody. Passado: broke; particípio: broken. Aparece muito com gently: break the news gently.

cards.definition: A polite phrase used right before you disagree with someone.
cards.example:
- With all due respect, I see the data differently.
Com todo o respeito, eu vejo os dados de forma diferente.
- With all due respect, that deadline was never realistic.
Com todo o respeito, aquele prazo nunca foi realista.
- He started three sentences with “with all due respect”, and nobody felt respected.
Ele começou três frases com “com todo o respeito”, e ninguém se sentiu respeitado.
cards.note: Anuncia discordância frontal — use com parcimônia, ou vira ataque educado. Alternativas mais leves: I see your point, but… e I may be missing something, but…

cards.definition: The act of making someone believe something that is not true.
cards.example:
- The audit revealed a deception, not a mistake.
A auditoria revelou uma fraude, não um erro.
- Hiding the real numbers from the board would be deception, not diplomacy.
Esconder os números reais do conselho seria fraude, não diplomacia.
- Investors sued the company for deception after the report came out.
Os investidores processaram a empresa por fraude depois que o relatório saiu.
cards.note: “Decepção” é disappointment: What a disappointment! Deception é o ato deliberado de enganar. Verbo: deceive; adjetivo: deceptive.

cards.definition: Not final yet, or said without full confidence.
cards.example:
- We set a tentative date: March 10, to be confirmed.
Marcamos uma data provisória: 10 de março, a confirmar.
- The agreement is tentative until legal reviews the last clause.
O acordo é provisório até o jurídico revisar a última cláusula.
- She gave a tentative answer because the numbers were still moving.
Ela deu uma resposta hesitante porque os números ainda estavam mudando.
cards.note: “Tentativa” é attempt e “tentador” é tempting. A tentative plan é um plano provisório. O advérbio tentatively significa provisoriamente: we tentatively agreed on Friday.

exercise.title: Diplomatic language & softening bad news (B2 · Aula 5)

questions.prompt: You want to present a delay as temporary and under control. Which word fits best?
questions.explanation: A “setback” delays progress; the other words suggest that everything failed.

questions.prompt: We are _____ over budget — three per cent, to be exact.
questions.explanation: “Slightly” softens the number without hiding it.

questions.prompt: Alguém precisa dar a notícia ao cliente antes de sexta.
questions.answer: Someone has to break the news to the client before Friday.|Someone needs to break the news to the client before Friday.
questions.explanation: “Break the news” means to be the first person to tell someone bad news.

questions.prompt: The report hid the real churn figures on purpose. What is that, in English?
questions.explanation: “Deception” is deliberate; “disappointment” is the false friend for “decepção”.

questions.prompt: The client took my email badly, so let me _____ the whole second paragraph.
questions.explanation: “Rephrase” means to say the same idea with different words.

questions.prompt: Com todo o respeito, eu discordo dessa conclusão.
questions.answer: With all due respect, I disagree with that conclusion.|With all due respect, I have to disagree with that conclusion.
questions.explanation: This phrase announces polite but direct disagreement.

questions.prompt: The date is already in the calendar, but it still has to be confirmed. How do you describe it?
Investors punish teams that _____ bad numbers instead of explaining them.
questions.explanation: “Downplay” means to present something as less serious than it is.

questions.prompt: Eu gostaria de levantar uma ressalva sobre o orçamento.
questions.answer: I would like to raise a concern about the budget.|I'd like to raise a concern about the budget.
questions.explanation: “Raise a concern” is the diplomatic way to open a disagreement.

questions.prompt: Which reply rejects a proposal in the most tactful way?
options: This plan will never work here.
This plan is simply wrong for us.
This plan makes no sense at all.
This plan may need a second look.
questions.answer: This plan may need a second look.
questions.explanation: Being “tactful” means saying the difficult thing without embarrassing anyone.
